question: Which Plate defaults and public plugin contracts serve a product job, and which duplicate an adequate Plite owner?
trigger: The owner asked for a best-api-review audit of every open ledger unit, frozen from status at fe0e9599a6 on 2026-10-04 (39 units), and judged afresh because earlier verdicts came from a weaker model. It asked for verdicts only, so no plan, build or panel follows in this run. This scope was open as pursue-unbound at queue position 6 in the plate-core group. It is not the unit next returned, which was reads.
requirements: Infer installed capabilities, dependencies, schema, reads, updates and services without caller annotations or casts.
One nominal descriptor identity and one installed owner across raw Plite, headless Plate and React Plate; reject unrelated same-name descriptors and preserve configured ancestry.
Plate keeps product authoring (ordered extend stages, terminal configure, stores, codecs, shortcuts, rendering); Plite plugins have no config (VISION.md:104, :126).
Required app resources cross an explicit options-to-plugin factory; configure and extend keep one job each.
Headless and static entrypoints never require React; static and RSC bind server-safe components.
Per-editor configuration and store isolation, atomic failed-candidate rollback and active-transaction ownership.
evidenceReuse: Reused the 2026-09-13 shared-identity production proof and the 2026-09-14 factory implementation proof as historical receipts, not rerun. Rechecked on the live tree that the deleted identity machinery is absent from packages/platejs/src and packages/plitejs/src, the single editor.plugin and tx.plugin portal in plitejs interfaces, YjsPlugin built by createPluginFactory and consumed through create, require and map in docs, copied UI, specs and type tests, getCorePlugins kept private, and Plate defaults (History, Transfer, DOM) that add Plate-configurable state or policy over Plite constructors.
summary: The job is for apps to compose plugin tuples and customize product policy, for authors to declare dependencies, schema, reads, updates, services and React presentation with inference, and for raw Plite to stay free of Plate's product grammar. Live source has no synthetic runtime descriptors, alias maps or name remaps (zero hits for extensionByName, registerEditorExtensionAlias, defineExtension and editor.extension( in either package's source). It has one editor.plugin(Descriptor) portal with 347 occurrences in the registry, tx.plugin inside transactions, and YjsPlugin as a non-installable factory used by docs, copied collaboration UI, specs and type tests. The strongest replacements, moving Plate's staged authoring and terminal configure into Plite or merging Base and React plugins, still break hard laws. Raw Plite has no consumer for product stages or config, and React fields would pull React types into the headless root. The small remaining debt, History and Transfer adapters cast to handwritten definitions, has no measured defect and does not earn a design change. Root VISION.md still teaches the deleted extension vocabulary (lines 99, 104, 105, 131). editor-public-naming carries that doctrine repair and distribution carries the Plite-root export leak, so no further plate-api work is justified.

alternatives: Keeping the current design is selected. Shared descriptor identity, Plate's product compiler, the editor.plugin and tx.plugin portal and mapped factories serve every current job with one installed owner.
Replacing the architecture by moving Plate's staged authoring and terminal configure into Plite loses. Raw Plite consumers have no job for it, and VISION.md:104 forbids plugin config in Plite.
Deleting or merging the Base and React split and toReactPlugin loses. React hooks, handlers and slots would put React types into the headless and static root and break dependency closure.

Deriving the History and Transfer wrappers through the factory witness to drop their as-unknown-as casts (HistoryPlugin.ts:51-52, TransferPlugin.ts:21-23) loses on value. The wrappers add Plate-configurable state, the mirrors reference Plite's own capability types, and the cast avoids a documented TypeScript blow-up with no observed defect.
Moving isNominalPluginDescriptor from the platejs root to platejs/compiler has no material benefit, with one CLI consumer and no confusion evidence.
Restoring separate plugin and extension portals, or a Plate installation map, loses. It recreates the second identity the production proof deleted.
proofLimits: Source inspection only; no tests, typecheck, build, browser or benchmark run. The factory and shared-identity proof receipts are historical from their records and were not replayed. packages/platejs/src/facade.ts and packages/platejs/src/lib/editor/withPlite.ts carry unstaged edits from other sessions; no decisive fact here rests on them. Core default membership, such as HtmlPlugin in every editor, was not re-judged; the html and conversion scopes own codec defaults.
